analysis.title: Credit Strategy Outlook 2027: Battle hardened
key_insights: SG expects credit markets to start 2027 under pressure with modestly wider spreads, driven by factors outside credit (Middle East war, oil, sovereign bond volatility). Those drivers should fade toward end of 2Q27, letting credit recover the lost ground.
SG recommends a defensive start to 2027, avoiding higher-beta sectors, then shifting to riskier bonds and sectors in 2H27. It frames 2027 as a year of two halves.

Spreads widened in Sep-Oct 2026: iBoxx Corporates from about B+90bp in late August to B+122.5bp two months later, and iTraxx Main from 50bp to 68bp (4bp of that from the September roll). The move is moderate by historical standards and has not reversed meaningfully.

2026 is set to be the first year since 2022 with credit spreads ending wider than they started. Total returns were hurt more than excess returns by the sovereign sell-off, and USD IG total returns contracted more sharply than euro IG despite milder spread widening.

Valuations have improved: the iBoxx Corporates spread is just below its long-term mean, ASW spread is well above its cycle mean, and iBoxx Corporates yield is the highest since January 2012. SG says yields give a strong reason to buy corporate bonds.

Corporate fundamentals remain solid. Earnings growth has been strong (6 straight quarters in Europe, 13 in the US), leverage is stable with no generalised releveraging outside AI hyperscalers, and Moody's rating drift ratio has been positive in Europe for 43 months. The US ratio turned positive in June 2026.
Default rates remain elevated but are falling: the US rate is around 5% (peak 6.4% in early 2025) and the European rate is just under 4%.

AI-related issuance was broadly in line with SG's USD estimate of $220-240bn but euro AI issuance came in at €44.5bn against a €100bn estimate. SG sees uncertainty over the AI industry after the US midterm results, and prefers an underweight on AI-related bonds regardless of rating.

SG's Credit Scorecard shows political risk as the main negative (impact -3), with corporate fundamentals, investor demand and supply supportive. Valuations are neutral to slightly negative. Overall average is 0.5, up 0.1 from 3 September.

Oil fell almost $20 on Brent and about $16 on WTI in four sessions after the US midterms on hopes of progress toward ending the Middle East war, but prices remain near $100/bbl. Global observed oil inventories fell by more than 500 million barrels since February per the IEA September report.

The 10y OAT-Bund spread rose from about 60bp in 1H26 to 174bp in the second half of October, and has since fallen toward 150bp. French elections in 2027 are expected to hold market attention, and SG sees the spread peak around that time.

Central banks started a new hiking cycle: the ECB hiked in June 2026 and the Fed in September. SG economists expect one more ECB hike by December and two Fed hikes (December and March), which would be less hawkish than market pricing.

SG forecasts iBoxx spreads to benchmarks: USD IG 105bp (4Q26), 115bp (1Q27), 125bp (2Q27), 130bp (3Q27), 125bp (4Q27). Euro IG 110bp, 120bp, 125bp, 120bp, 110bp. USD HY 370bp, 400bp, 450bp, 475bp, 475bp. Euro HY 390bp, 430bp, 460bp, 450bp, 420bp. Spot on 6 November: USD IG 108bp, EUR IG 117bp, USD HY 353bp, EUR HY 397bp.

SG expects the turning point for euro credit around mid-2Q27 and the peak near the French elections. USD indices should do better near term as they are further from the sources of weakness, but US companies are expected to releverage earlier, so USD IG underperforms EUR IG in 2H27. USD HY is expected to underperform other indices.

Sector positioning for the start of 2027: overweight senior financials (bank bail-in, senior preferred, senior insurance, financial services senior), neutral/underweight across others, with underweight on AI-related bonds, other triple-Bs except high triple-B, and single-Bs versus double-Bs. Overweight double-A and single-A. SG expects Financials to underperform Non-financials in a widening environment since they are high-beta.

Curves: SG expects both Financial and Non-financial credit curves to bear-flatten in early 2027, with the short end widening faster. Year-to-date the short end widened about 28bp against 21bp for the long end.
For the second half of 2027, SG shifts to higher-beta sectors (subordinated financials, Tier 2, AT1, hybrids, real estate) as spreads are expected to stabilise and improve after 2Q.

Euro issuance is above €800bn and should reach about €900bn in 2026 (a third straight record), with USD issuance about $1.945tn heading above $2tn. SG expects a fourth consecutive record in 2027. Euro IG non-financials issuance is at €400.9bn, 7.5% above last year, heading to about €430bn in 2026 and €450bn in 2027.

Euro HY issuance should reach €130-140bn in 2027, testing the 2021 record of €133bn. Senior financials should grow towards €260bn, the best year since 2007. Sub-financials should return to about €80bn after about €70bn in 2026. Green issuance should end 2026 near €170bn and rise to €180bn or more in 2027.

Coupon payments in 2027 are forecast at €124bn for euro indices (+19%) and $537bn for USD indices (+13%), supporting investor demand. Insurers' target yields are below government yields, but insurers remain active in credit.

Risks: a continued Middle East war with oil rising, a rapid rise in sovereign yields (SG Rates sees the 10y Bund at 3.75-3.85% in 1H27, and the speed of the rise matters more than the level), and a recession, which SG considers very unlikely but would push spreads to 1Q23 (post-Credit Suisse) wides.

sector_views.sector: Senior Financials (bank bail-in, senior preferred, senior insurance, financial services)
sector_views.rationale: Seen as the safest part of the credit universe for a defensive start to 2027, though they may widen as Financials remain high-beta.
In a spread-widening environment in 1H27, Financials are expected to underperform Non-financials because of their high beta.
Heavy new issue volumes are expected to weigh on existing bonds regardless of rating.
Listed as underweight in the start-of-year table, linked to heavy AI-related supply and uncertainty over the AI industry.

sector_views.sector: Automobiles, Basic Resources, Chemicals, Construction & Materials, Media, Retail, Telecommunications, Travel & Leisure
sector_views.rationale: Higher-beta and cyclical sectors are avoided at the start of 2027 in the defensive posture.

sector_views.sector: Utilities, Industrial Goods & Services, Health Care, Food & Beverage, Oil & Gas, Personal & Household Goods
sector_views.rationale: Neutral positioning in the start-of-year table.

sector_views.sector: Subordinated financials (Tier 2, AT1 CoCos, Corporate Hybrids, Sub Ins, Real Estate)
sector_views.rationale: Moved to overweight for 2H27 as spreads are expected to stabilise and improve after 2Q, favouring higher-beta sectors.

earnings_insights: Companies on both sides of the Atlantic have posted strong earnings growth for 6 straight quarters in Europe and 13 in the US, and most companies keep beating expectations. The report gives no specific EPS figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Positive but not strong enough to push companies into aggressive releveraging, which is benign for credit.
Moderate growth supports credit fundamentals. The eurozone recently surprised to the upside.
Inflation is expected to ease from the 2026 oil-driven spike, though it stays above 2% target.
Inflation stays above the 2% target in 2027, supporting further central bank tightening.

macro_indicators.reading: Two further Fed hikes expected by SG economists, in December 2026 and March 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: SG's expected path is a little less hawkish than market pricing, which has almost two hikes priced.

macro_indicators.reading: One more ECB hike by December 2026 expected by SG economists; market prices two
macro_indicators.interpretation: The ECB started hiking in June 2026.
The speed of the rise matters more for credit than the level. An orderly rise lets spreads hold or tighten.

macro_indicators.reading: 174bp peak in second half of October 2026, about 150bp at time of writing
macro_indicators.interpretation: Close to the worst levels since 2011, with French elections in 2027 a focal risk. French senior bank yields narrowed to zero spread versus the 5y OAT.

trade_ideas.description: Start 2027 overweight double-A and single-A rated bonds, neutral high triple-B and underweight other triple-B bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: A defensive stance for the expected spread widening in 1H27.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight senior financials (senior preferred bank bonds, NPS, senior insurance, financial services) versus Non-financials for defensive start, then shift to higher-beta sectors in 2H27
trade_ideas.rationale: Senior financials are seen as the safest part of the credit universe, with higher-beta sectors expected to recover once spreads stabilise after 2Q27.
trade_ideas.risk: Financials remain high-beta and could widen with the market.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight single-Bs and lower-rated bonds versus double-Bs in HY; underweight EUR HY versus IG and USD HY versus USD IG
trade_ideas.rationale: Lower-rated bonds are expected to widen faster in a volatile, widening environment.
trade_ideas.risk: USD HY proved the most resilient index in 2026 despite the same view being held.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight AI-related bonds regardless of rating
trade_ideas.rationale: Heavy new issue volumes are expected to weigh on existing bonds.

trade_ideas.description: Bear-flattening of credit curves in early 2027, with the short end widening faster than the long end
trade_ideas.rationale: The short end is expected to widen faster in the spread pressure early in the year, while the long end outperforms in relative terms.

trade_ideas.description: Long iTraxx protection (hedge) suggested in late September 2026
trade_ideas.rationale: Hedge against rising risk aversion given lack of visibility.

risk_factors: The Middle East war continues or deteriorates, with oil rising further, supply chain disruption and a bigger hit to the economy.
A rapid rise in sovereign bond yields with a sharp increase in uncertainty, particularly if oil surges again.
An economic recession (very low probability) that would push spreads toward the 1Q23 wides after the Credit Suisse collapse.
Political risk from the French and Italian elections in 2027, with French OAT-Bund spread near its worst levels since 2011.
Uncertainty over the AI industry after the US midterm results, and heavy AI-related issuance.
Earlier US corporate releveraging as better US economic prospects could push USD IG wider in 2H27.
Private credit woes and high sovereign debt trajectories.
vol_and_positioning: One-month realised volatility in credit rose moderately in Sep-Oct 2026, below the levels after the start of the Middle East war and well below the levels after the 2025 US tariff announcements.
The iBoxx Corporates spread range so far in 2026 is the lowest since 2021 and the third lowest since 2013.
SG suggested hedging rising risk aversion by buying iTraxx protection in late September 2026.
Credit Sharpe ratios are more attractive than those of sovereign bonds, and SG does not expect a significant rise in volatility in 2027.
New issue premiums rose from late March/April and again from September onwards, but deals were well received and oversubscribed.
geopolitical: War in the Middle East (referred to as war in Iran) is pushing up oil prices and disrupting supply chains. Hopes of resolution rose after the US midterm elections gave Democrats full control of Congress.
US midterm results have raised questions about the future of the AI industry.
Trade and tariff discussions continue, with persistent tensions between the US and Canada and talk of Canada becoming an associate member of the EU.
French and Italian elections in 2027, with the French election seen as most market-relevant given the OAT-Bund spread.

tension_points.bull_case: Solid corporate fundamentals (strong earnings, stable leverage, positive rating drift), strong investor demand with record issuance absorbed, highest yields since 2012 and a better Sharpe ratio than sovereigns should let spreads tighten from late 2Q27.
tension_points.bear_case: Middle East war and oil near $100, volatile sovereign yields (Bund seen at 3.75-3.85% in 1H27), French elections and AI uncertainty should push spreads wider in 1H27, with USD companies releveraging earlier.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Clear progress toward ending the Middle East war and sovereign bond markets finding a new floor would bring the recovery forward. A very rapid rise in sovereign yields with a sharp rise in uncertainty, or a recession, would break the mild-widening view.
